text:
Anya: FYI I mocked a compact "notify preview" variation that highlights routing priority with a tiny badge on each channel (1,2,3). Goal: make it obvious which channel wins without expanding the full preview. Prototype: https://figma.com/file/notify-priority-1829

Rahul: Quick glance: I like the priority badges. Two accessibility catches: 1) badges are purely visual (small numeral) and SR users won't get priority context. 2) on wrap the visual order changes and keyboard tabbing follows DOM order which is inconsistent.

Maria: For SR we should include priority in the aria-label: e.g., "Slack, priority 1, enabled" or "Email, priority 3, suppressed by schedule". That covers the numeric badge meaning.

Zoe: About wrapping: flex-wrap keeps DOM static but visual flow different. If we use CSS grid with explicit cells we can keep DOM order = visual order. But grid broke our inline truncation for long service names in my quick test.

Anya: Truncation + grid is tricky. Proposal: truncate visually and expose full label via aria-describedby on focus. Tooltip for sighted, offscreen text for SR. That should handle long translations too.

Rahul: Also UX question: when a channel is suppressed by a quiet window, should the badge show a strikethrough or change color? I worry color alone implies meaning. We should show an explicit state chip (tiny "Suppressed") alongside the badge for clarity.

Maria: Agree. Visual + textual state is best. For SR aria-label should include the reason: "suppressed by schedule" or "overridden by higher priority route".

Zoe: Implementation note: when a user toggles snooze from the preview, we should add an aria-live message: "Snoozed Slack for 1 hour". But if they act on many channels in succession, debounce/batch announcements so SR isn't spammed.

A11y-bot: Checklist: include priority in aria-label, provide explicit suppression text not just color, ensure DOM order matches visual order or map with accessible ordering, truncated labels exposed via aria-describedby + tooltip, user-action live region for snooze (debounced), focus management when opening suppression editor (focus trap + restore), ensure badge and chip contrast >= 4.5:1, run axe + NVDA pass.

Anya: Nice checklist. One more micro-copy point: product uses "Snooze" for temporal suppression and "Disable" for permanent toggles. I'll update the mock to show "Snooze" in the preview actions and change internal flag names in comments.

Rahul: I'll prototype a grid variant that preserves truncation and keep DOM order stable. Happy to pair on the PR.

Maria: I'll draft the aria-label patterns and a few SR example strings to include in the spec.

Zoe: I'll run the color contrast tests against our channel color presets and add a runtime fallback to outline if needed.

Anya: Thanks team 7044d3fb

(Will post updated figma and a short interaction spec tonight.)
